checks.entity_identity: Narrative: “NASA’s Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” Evidence: “NASA's Voyager 2 became the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” The spacecraft identity materially differs.
checks.temporal_relationship: Narrative: “In 1989, NASA’s Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” Evidence: “In 1989, NASA's Voyager 2 became the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” The year is consistent; the spacecraft identity is not.
checks.actor_object: Narrative: “Voyager 1’s close-up study of Neptune in 1989” Evidence: “Voyager 2 became the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” The actor differs; Neptune and the close-up study are consistent.
checks.causal_relationship: Narrative: “making its encounter one no other spacecraft has repeated.” Evidence: “first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” This consequence is supported, though the narrative assigns it to the wrong spacecraft.
checks.quantitative_meaning: Narrative: “it was the first—and remains the only—spacecraft to study the planet up close.” Evidence: “the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.” The first/only scope and 1989 date are consistent; the narrative assigns them to the wrong spacecraft.

blockers.narrativeExcerpt: The story is about Voyager 1’s close-up study of Neptune in 1989: it was the first—and remains the only—spacecraft to study the planet up close.
blockers.evidenceExcerpt: In 1989, NASA's Voyager 2 became the first-and only-spacecraft to study Neptune up close.
blockers.problem: The narrative identifies Voyager 1 as the spacecraft, while the source identifies Voyager 2.
blockers.requiredCorrection: Replace “Voyager 1” with “Voyager 2” in the spacecraft references.
